cases.name: Stella Marcella Savas Anderson
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Stella was the middle child of three. When she was very young the family moved to North Fork Township in Kanabec County. She attended country school and Ogilvie High School.

Stella fell in love with the outdoors. She especially loved wildlife and feeding her pets (wild birds), trees, flowers, vegetable gardening, picking berries, canning, fishing and hunting — all of which she knew very much about and could educate you in at any time.

“Let’s not forget about her love for dancing.”

She had many losses, hardships and heartaches throughout life — losing three of her children being the worst, but she persevered and kept on dancing.

Stella wasn’t a person you would see in a pew on Sundays at church, but she had a strong relationship with God. She spoke of him often and prayed. That is how she got through her grief. She was never a preacher but a believer.


advertisement
Stella started working at a young age being a nanny and housecleaner for a wealthy family in Minneapolis. That is where she got her passion for cooking, decorating and keeping her home spotless. She worked various jobs throughout her life, but her two favorites were Lindy Little Joes in Isle and Lifetouch National School Studio in Bloomington.

Throughout her life she had some wonderful, very close friends. She treasured her time with them like her memorable trip to Hawaii with Jane and Carlene. If Stella was your friend, or someone she cared deeply for, she would give and help you in any way she could, even if it meant her going without.

She loved her family, friends and her little dog, Bella, dearly. She has left behind broken hearts and a void in so many of us, but she also leaves behind many fun, wonderful and cherished memories."
cases.narrative: An autopsy conducted by the coroner’s office determined that her manner of death was a homicide caused by “horrific sharp force injuries” that included “seven cuts to her head from a tomahawk type hatchet."
